messages.text:
Implemented the Python eza port for the requested benchmark surface.

Changed files:
- `eza_port.py:145` CLI parser and option behavior
- `eza_port.py:328` filesystem entry model
- `eza_port.py:505` Windows long-view permission/attribute rendering
- `eza_port.py:585` long/details rendering
- `eza_port.py:616` tree traversal/rendering
- `eza_port.py:640` input path handling, stdout/stderr/status behavior
- `eza_port.py:701` main entrypoint
- `executable:4` Python runnable entrypoint importing `eza_port.main`
- `compile.sh:3` removes stale higher-priority entrypoints
- `compile.sh:7` validates Python syntax
- `.tura/script/diff_verify.py:39` generated valid oracle samples
- `.tura/script/diff_verify.py:58` generated invalid oracle samples

Validation:
- `python -m py_compile eza_port.py executable .tura\script\diff_verify.py` passed.
- `python .tura\script\diff_verify.py` passed: `ok 20 generated oracle comparisons`.
- Applicable original-test audit passed: 71 selected behavior-area cases, 0 failures.
- Manual smoke checks passed for:
  - `python .\executable --version`
  - `python .\executable rust-reference\tests\itest --color never --icons never --oneline`
  - `python .\executable rust-reference\tests\itest --color never --icons never --long --no-user --no-time`
  - `python .\executable rust-reference\tests\itest --color never --icons never --tree --level 2`
  - invalid sort behavior returns status 3 with matching stderr.

One environment note:
- I could not execute `./compile.sh` locally because this Windows image has no usable `sh`/`bash` (`sh` not found; WSL launcher has no `/bin/bash`). I validated the same compile action directly with `python -m py_compile`. The `compile.sh` file is present and idempotent.
